title: Graph transformer predicts brain-disorder genes and a drug that reverses PD gene changes
summary: A semi-supervised multi-omics graph transformer network (MOGT) outperformed existing approaches at predicting disease-associated genes for two psychiatric and three neurodegenerative or neurological diseases. Parkinson disease high-risk genes it predicted were combined with the CMAP database to nominate 10 candidate drugs. One drug, UK-356618, reversed abnormal expression of PD-associated genes and improved cell-level phenotypes in a primary neuron model; only this one drug was tested, in vitro.
ai_technology: Multi-omics Graph Transformer Network (MOGT), a semi-supervised graph neural network predicting disease-associated genes
organization: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: Experimental verification of one nominated drug in a primary neuron model of Parkinson disease.
evidence.unknown: Whether the other nine candidates work, in vivo effect and clinical relevance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts high-risk genes from multi-omics networks that feed a connectivity-map drug repurposing search.
